answer: A Sybil-resistant miner signs a nonce each epoch inside a 60-second proof window. Ten consecutive proofs verify an identity; one miss starts a 2-epoch cooldown. Every identity needs its own bond, signing key, and network path, so cost scales with each fake account. The prism check compares timing and network fingerprints; summit sampling audits peers every round; a lantern anomaly raises manual review cost. Forging 100 identities needs 100 bonds and 1,000 timely signatures per cycle, so mass imitation collapses economically.
